items.title: Worthia "Showboy" Thomas Interview, 1961-12-11
items.q: at that time, the most playing that we done in that band was the music we played for the show... this professor, Professor Randolph, he had pretty good ideas about jazz then at that time, because he was writing some arrangements, that is, for the bands to do specialists.

ctx.x: How did they play? Did you notice any difference in their style? Did they play much jazz or mostly just other songs for the show?

Or how? Well, at that time, the most playing that we done in that band was the music we played for the show, for the performers. And well this professor, Professor Randolph, he had pretty good ideas about jazz then at that time, because he was writing some arrangements, that is, for the bands to do specialists. Had special spots along during the show that the band would do specialists. Well he had wrote some nice stuff for a band to do specialists.

Roofing Randolph, I forget his first name, had worked with Louis Armstrong later, and he wrote to old man Moe. He says, Randolph, I used to hear him in Chicago. He'd been with Armstrong for a while, sort of organized his band, played second trumpet with him. Well this Randolph was a violin player. Oh no, this was a trumpet player.
